MID-CYCLE MANUAL RUN: judgment written 2026-08-26, five calendar days after the 2026-08-21 close this file reads. Two of the five sessions in the week window (Mon 08-24, Tue 08-25) had already traded. The three catalysts that dominate the window -- July core PCE and NVDA earnings (both 08-26), and the Warsh Jackson Hole keynote (08-28) -- were all still ahead, and the pinned research snapshot (2026-08-24) carries no post-08-21 outcomes. The week horizon is still not a clean ex-ante forecast and must not be graded as one.

why: Utilities are the worst-positioned sector in this run on both axes: +8.6 pct absolute and -22.7 pts excess in archetype 1, and the most negative long-rate beta of the eleven at -0.50 to the 30Y, into a 10Y closing at a 52-week high (The Full Regime-Sector Matrix; Sector Macro Sensitivity Matrix; wiki/economic-calendar.md@63b4d3ba).

The rate-to-margin channel is documented for Utilities specifically and it runs the wrong way: industry interest expense rose 34.4 pct in 2023 against only 11 bps of awarded-ROE relief, so higher rates compress the sector through debt service with regulatory lag (Sector Macro Sensitivity Matrix).
risks: XLU -3.48 pct crashed through both its 50D and 200D, marked a trend change to bearish with dividend-focused retail likely capitulating; $75 is the level below which the pair trade against XLRE stops being a pair (wiki/synthesis.md@cd85b433).

why: The panel corroborates hard: -7.58 pts vs SPY on the month, the worst of the eleven, with 0.0 breadth on the week -- not a single constituent posted a positive return (panel metrics, this file).
The same 10Y move that hurt Utilities left XLRE nearly flat, isolating duration and regulatory lag rather than a general defensive de-rating as the mechanism (wiki/synthesis.md@cd85b433).
risks: This is the most one-sided reading in the run, which is itself the risk: a dovish Warsh keynote on 08-28 that hands the market its discount rate back would reverse the duration trade fastest here (wiki/economic-calendar.md@63b4d3ba).
